The lyre guitar is a guitar shaped like a lyre, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.322-5. It has six single strings and a fingerboard between two curved arms, close in shape to the ancient Greek kithara; it is tuned and played like a traditional guitar, and usually has a built-in stand so that it can be stood upright when not in use. From the late eighteenth to the early nineteenth century it was fashionable in Parisian high society as a salon instrument; Marie Antoinette played it, and fashionable women also posed with it as if playing an ancient Greek kithara.
